author: David Geddes
text: • Admin • 1yr What should you know about "? First there are two competing architectures. We call them \"chained\" or \"integrated\"" 1. *Chained* are rule-based agents. These are very common and have been for a long long time. Rules help agents pass-off tasks to the next widget based on monotonic triggers - chained rules. Do you have one in your home like Alexa? or Google Home? You still have to train the language models, requires a lot of computing power for a small bump, est. .3% productivity, a very low 1% ROI. There are objective reasons for the limitations like physics. 2. *Integrated* are knowledge-based agents. These are not very common and sit on top of your business knowledge. This type can integrate a half dozen techniques to understand your intent and help you achieve your goals without asking for help [query]. Productivity increases for these types of agents can be 10% with a 30% ROI. The challenge is designing the graph structure and adding the math.
